The 16x crop shows the 10uH's final coil stroke overshooting downward to x~417,y~713 where it grazes the rail, while the actual connecting wire leaves the same point as a big hop arc that goes round the rail and down to the 50uF top plate. I read the overshoot as pen follow-through, not a tap: S32 = 'none' so the lead tip is not welded to the rail, S33 = [[57,64],[59,65]] (rail e57-e64 straight through; arc e59-e65 straight through), S34 = junction (rail continues into e66). Treating the overshoot as a junction would put 10uH bottom and 50uF top both on R4 and destroy the private node n5.

 (g) S49 (416,889) - CROSSING, and this is the one real judgement call. Here C3's tail and the bottom rail R6 form a plain X (both wires continue on both sides). A junction reading ties R5 to R6; R6 is already tied to R4 by C2's tail (S30/S47), so R4=R5=R6 and V-DC 15V #11 would be short-circuited (and I-DC #8 too) - electrically impossible, which per the tie-break rules settles it. Consequence of the crossing: GND ends up on the R5 node with the I-DC bottom, the V-DC 15V top and the 50uF bottom - a 4-terminal net.
